analysis:
Examined all four primary analyses and the supplied source replay independently. The ci.yml patch adds conditional macOS lanes at HEAD 53–64 and routes provider shards/summary/SDK and cluster metadata/runtime/GPU/focused jobs through route outputs (234, 479, 677, 880, 1012, 1074, 1136). Lane predicates match the visible job conditions, and each matrix shard has its own lane. The patch does not change test commands, cache-save rules, token permissions or aggregate result checks; incomplete replay limits independent verification of surrounding controls and test assertions.
The build.md patch (HEAD 253–301) and changelog.d/ci-macos-darkbloom-route.md:3–6 describe exact-label grants, Blacksmith fallback, same-repository admission and unchanged literal runners for release/signing. These descriptions are not proof of provisioning controls. No supplied source establishes an authorization bypass, plaintext disclosure, billing change or weakened runtime/cache encryption; TB-002, TB-011 and T-041 production behavior is not modified here. CI success must remain distinct from signed-artifact and physical-host qualification under A-017/T-054/T-056.
The material unresolved question is the newly eligible macOS runner trust boundary: verify darkbloom-route.yml and the plane/Sandbox contract for runner ownership, host/guest isolation, cleanup between PRs and trusted pushes, lane binding and lease lifetime for delayed summary jobs. Determine whether these runners can access owner credentials/live provider data (A-019/A-008/A-001), contaminate trusted-branch caches or supply evidence used for qualification (ADV-001/TB-003/A-017). Neither provider-controlled execution nor a missing isolation control is established, so these are review questions, not findings. Source replay omits 12 reviewed units, including test implementation context; reconcile scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py and scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py against actual routing behavior. No independently supported regression warrants a finding in the supplied evidence.
